goal.source_text: Maximize this rocket fin's stability, keep drag low, keep it under 40 g, must fit a 3-inch body tube.

constraints.label: Fins must not overhang the aft end

assumptions: The 40 g limit applies to all fins combined (fin_mass_total_g), since no per-fin qualifier was given.
The 3-inch body tube (76.2 mm) is the mounting body for the fins and does not limit any fin dimension.
Maximize stability is interpreted as targeting about 2.5 calibers, since a larger margin would weathercock the rocket.
Keeping drag low is interpreted as minimizing total fin-set drag at the 120 m/s design velocity given in the context.
Fin count is left free (3 or 4) since the goal does not specify it.
Read '3-inch body tube' as the rocket body: 76.2 mm diameter, fins may not overhang the aft end.

message.body:
Relative to the seed, the champion dropped fin count from 4 to 3, shortened root chord from 90 to 66 mm, lengthened semi-span from 60 to 68 mm, and reduced sweep from 30 to 22 degrees. This brought fin mass from 60.264 g to 38.817 g, which clears the 40 g limit the seed violated, and drag fell from 9.783 N to 8.514 N. The cost is stability, which moved from 2.23 to 1.926 cal, further below the 2.5 cal target but still within the 1.0 tolerance. Physically, fewer, higher-aspect fins shed mass and wetted area while the longer span recovers some normal-force effectiveness. On the same 64-evaluation budget, CMA-ES reached an aggregate of 0.5846 versus the agent's 0.5819, so it matched or marginally beat the agent, with a four-fin design that has a higher flutter margin (1.912 vs 1.562) but is heavier at 39.664 g.
